display.title: The Secret Tunnel
display.summary_short: An old shammes finally reveals why he polishes the shul's great brass menorah so lovingly: long ago it opened a secret tunnel that saved the whole congregation.
display.summary_long: A Chanukah story from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Reb Beryl, the very old shammes of the shul, keeps Hashem's house spotless, and gives special care to the huge, beautifully engraved brass menorah beside the Aron HaKodesh. When people ask why, he only smiles and says, 'Someday I'll tell you.' At last he tells his secret. When he was young, cruel people tried to stop the Jews from learning Torah, and bands of hooligans attacked the shul. One day an armed mob surrounded it, and their leader gave the worshippers ten minutes to say their last prayers. The rabbi said Tehillim, then turned one of the menorah's brass arms, and a hidden door opened onto a tunnel that led to the edge of the city. Everyone escaped, and the hooligans, finding the shul empty, fled in fright, crying that it was haunted. That is why Reb Beryl treasures the menorah: through it, with Hashem's help, his life was saved.
display.lesson: Hashem saves His people in wondrous ways, and we should treasure and care for the things of our shul.

date.note: Cut from episode 354 (dated 12-06-88), told 'in honor of Chanukah'; the same story also aired in episodes 155 and 506.

advisories.note: Armed hooligans surround a shul and threaten to kill the worshippers; past attacks cost innocent lives.
Jews were prevented from learning Torah and keeping mitzvos.
